topics.name: Othello
topics.kicker: Shakespeare’s tragedy of the Moor of Venice · Jealousy turned fatal
topics.briefing: A celebrated Venetian general secretly marries Desdemona, the woman he loves, only to watch his own trusted officer poison his mind with jealousy. Using nothing but a dropped handkerchief and a string of lies, the villain Iago convinces the general that his new wife has betrayed him. By the play’s final scene, Shakespeare’s study of jealousy has destroyed nearly everyone on stage.

qb.tip: Only 2 Middle School/Easy High School tossups exist; 8 more real tossups turned up at Regular High School difficulty, so this sample leans harder on that pool than most topics.

sample.note: 10 real QBReader tossups (2 Middle School/Easy High School + 8 Regular High School, power-marked)

tossups.p: Brabantio accuses this man of using witchcraft to win his daughter’s heart, but the Venetian Senate lets their marriage stand after hearing the couple describe their courtship. The Senate then sends this man to defend Cyprus from a Turkish fleet that a storm destroys before any battle begins.
tossups.r: This man’s ensign tricks him into believing his bride has betrayed him using a dropped handkerchief as false proof. For 10 points, name this Shakespearean general who smothers his wife Desdemona in a jealous rage.

tossups.p: This man explains to the Venetian Senate that he won his wife’s love only through stories of his travels and battles, not through sorcery. His ensign resents being passed over for a promotion that instead goes to a less experienced officer named Cassio.
tossups.r: That ensign gets Cassio drunk and provokes a brawl that costs Cassio his rank. For 10 points, name this Shakespearean tragic hero, a Venetian general undone by jealousy.

tossups.p: A rejected suitor named Roderigo pays this man’s scheming ensign for help winning the woman this man has just married. That ensign later convinces Cassio to beg this man’s wife to plead his case, then twists their private meetings into “evidence” of an affair.
tossups.r: This man was given a handkerchief, supposedly woven by a sibyl and dyed in mummy, which he passed on to his wife as his first gift to her. For 10 points, name this general who demands his wife produce that handkerchief as proof of her faithfulness.

tossups.p: This man’s wife drops an heirloom handkerchief, which her attendant Emilia finds and gives to her own husband without realizing his intentions. That husband plants the handkerchief in Cassio’s room, and Cassio passes it on to his mistress, Bianca.
tossups.r: This man watches a conversation between Cassio and Iago that he is tricked into believing is about his own wife. For 10 points, name this jealous Shakespearean general.

tossups.p: In one scene, this man’s ensign warns him to beware “the green-eyed monster,” feeding suspicions that his wife has been unfaithful. That ensign had earlier wondered aloud in a soliloquy, “And what’s he then that says I play the villain?”
tossups.r: Consumed by jealousy, this man strikes his wife in public and calls her foul names in front of a visiting Venetian nobleman. For 10 points, name this Shakespearean general who later smothers that wife in their bed.

tossups.p: Before her death, this man’s wife sings a sad song that she learned from her mother’s maid, Barbary. This man’s ensign had earlier convinced a rejected suitor named Roderigo to ambush the newly demoted Cassio.
tossups.r: That ensign then killed Roderigo to silence him. For 10 points, name this Shakespearean general who smothers his own wife, Desdemona, believing she betrayed him.

tossups.p: After this man kills his wife, Emilia bursts in and reveals that she unknowingly gave the fatal handkerchief to her husband, exposing his lies. Iago stabs Emilia to keep her quiet, but the truth still reaches this man.
tossups.r: Realizing his fatal mistake, this man delivers a final speech recalling his years of service before killing himself with a hidden weapon. For 10 points, name this tragic Shakespearean general, the title character of a play set partly in Cyprus.

tossups.p: This man’s new bride is the daughter of a Venetian senator named Brabantio, who is said to have died of grief over the marriage before the play ends. A Venetian nobleman named Lodovico later arrives from Venice carrying letters that recall this man and name Cassio governor of Cyprus.
tossups.r: This man had governed Cyprus after replacing a man named Montano. For 10 points, name this Shakespearean general whose ensign Iago destroys his marriage out of resentment.

tossups.p: This man’s final speech recalls killing a Turk who had beaten a Venetian in the city of Aleppo. Before that, this man’s loyal lieutenant Cassio was demoted after a drunken brawl engineered by this man’s ensign.
tossups.r: This man was falsely convinced that his wife Desdemona had been unfaithful with that same lieutenant. For 10 points, name this Shakespearean general who smothers his wife and then takes his own life.

tossups.p: The actor Paul Robeson famously played the title role of this play on Broadway in a landmark production. This play’s plot is thought to be based on an Italian tale sometimes called “A Moorish Captain,” by the writer Cinthio [“SIN-tee-oh”].
tossups.r: Its main character is convinced by a dropped handkerchief that his wife has betrayed him. For 10 points, name this Shakespearean tragedy whose jealous general smothers his wife, Desdemona.

tossups.p: This play’s villain, an ensign passed over for a promotion, recruits a rejected suitor named Roderigo to help ruin the marriage at this play’s center. That villain’s own wife, Emilia, unknowingly hands him the handkerchief that seals the tragedy.
tossups.r: This play’s protagonist smothers his wife in their bed after being deceived by that ensign. For 10 points, name this Shakespearean tragedy set partly in Venice and partly in Cyprus.

tossups.p: In this play, a Venetian senator named Brabantio accuses the protagonist of using witchcraft to win his daughter’s love. A storm destroys an invading Turkish fleet early in this play, shifting its focus away from war and toward the protagonist’s marriage.
tossups.r: The protagonist’s ensign convinces him that his bride has been unfaithful with his own lieutenant, Cassio. For 10 points, name this Shakespearean tragedy whose title general smothers his wife, Desdemona.

tossups.p: This play’s villain gets the protagonist’s lieutenant drunk, provoking a brawl that costs him his rank and sets the villain’s revenge in motion. That villain later tells the protagonist to beware “the green-eyed monster” of jealousy.
tossups.r: The protagonist’s wife is smothered after a dropped handkerchief convinces him of her guilt. For 10 points, name this Shakespearean tragedy featuring a scheming ensign who destroys his general’s marriage.

tossups.p: This play’s subplot follows a jilted suitor named Roderigo, who pays the villain for help and is later killed by him to cover his tracks. The villain’s wife, Emilia, is murdered after she exposes her husband’s scheme to the protagonist.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this Shakespearean tragedy in which a Venetian general smothers his wife after believing his ensign’s lies about her faithfulness.

tossups.p: Early in this play, the protagonist defends his marriage before the Venetian Senate after his new father-in-law accuses him of sorcery. Its villain is driven partly by resentment at being passed over for a promotion given to a less experienced officer, Cassio.
tossups.r: Its heroine, Desdemona, is smothered in her bed after a missing handkerchief convinces her husband of her unfaithfulness. For 10 points, name this Shakespearean tragedy, perhaps literature’s most famous study of jealousy.

clues.t: Smothers his wife, Desdemona, in their bed after being deceived about her faithfulness
A tragedy by William Shakespeare, first performed in 1604
His ensign, Iago, manipulates him into a jealous rage out of resentment and ambition
A dropped handkerchief is used as false proof that his wife has been unfaithful
After learning the truth, he kills himself with a hidden weapon
Cassio, a less experienced officer, is promoted to lieutenant over Iago, fueling Iago’s resentment
Set partly in Venice and partly in Cyprus, where he governs after replacing Montano
Brabantio, his wife’s father, accuses him of witchcraft before the Venetian Senate
Emilia, Iago’s wife, unknowingly gives him the handkerchief, then is killed after exposing his scheme
Iago gets his lieutenant drunk, provoking a brawl that costs the man his military rank
A rejected suitor, Roderigo, pays Iago for help and is later killed by him
Iago warns him to beware “the green-eyed monster” of jealousy
He defends himself before the Senate by explaining he won his wife through stories of his travels, not sorcery
A storm destroys an invading Turkish fleet near Cyprus before any battle is fought
Cassio gives the planted handkerchief to his mistress, Bianca, unaware of Iago’s trap
His wife sings a sad song she learned from her mother’s maid, Barbary, shortly before her death
In a soliloquy, Iago wonders, “And what’s he then that says I play the villain?”
Consumed by jealousy, he strikes his wife and calls her foul names in front of the visiting Venetian Lodovico
The actor Paul Robeson famously played the title role in a landmark Broadway production
The plot is thought to come from an Italian tale sometimes called “A Moorish Captain,” by the writer Cinthio
His final speech recalls killing a Turk who had beaten a Venetian in the city of Aleppo
His wife’s father, Brabantio, is said to have died of grief over the marriage

trap.title: Othello or Iago?
trap.body: Most of this tossup’s clues describe scheming, lying, and manipulating — planting the handkerchief, stoking jealousy, destroying a marriage. Those are all things the villain Iago does, not the title character, so “Iago” is the single most tempting wrong buzz on this line.
trap.fix: Ask who the clue is happening TO, not who is doing the scheming. A clue about someone being deceived, growing jealous, or smothering his wife is about the general; save “Iago” for clues that describe the schemer himself.
trap.line: Real answer line: Othello, the Moor of Venice.

topics.name: The Scarlet Letter
topics.kicker: Hawthorne’s novel of Puritan Boston · Sin, shame, and secrecy
topics.briefing: In Puritan Boston, Hester Prynne is forced to wear a scarlet “A” on her dress as punishment for having a child with a man who is not her husband. Nathaniel Hawthorne’s novel follows her daughter, Pearl, the mysterious physician Roger Chillingworth, and the guilt-ridden minister Arthur Dimmesdale as their secrets slowly come undone.

qb.tip: All 8 real tossups are Middle School/Easy High School, but most lean on Mistress Hibbins’s forest invitation and the meteor/Governor Winthrop scene rather than on Dimmesdale or Chillingworth by name.

sample.note: the 8 real QBReader tossups for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked)

tossups.p: This novel’s introductory essay, “The Custom-House,” claims that its author discovered a faded cloth emblem and an old manuscript while working at a Salem customhouse. Its heroine is first displayed on a scaffold holding her infant daughter before a crowd of Puritan onlookers.
tossups.r: That heroine must wear a mark of her sin, which she has embroidered herself. For 10 points, name this Nathaniel Hawthorne novel about Hester Prynne.

tossups.p: Mistress Hibbins, rumored to be a witch, invites this novel’s heroine to join a witches’ gathering in the forest outside town. Years later, that heroine meets her former lover in that same forest and briefly unpins her hair and removes her badge of shame.
tossups.r: Her daughter, Pearl, often plays alone near their isolated cottage. For 10 points, name this novel in which Hester Prynne raises her daughter alone in Puritan Boston.

tossups.p: Governor Winthrop’s death coincides with the sighting of a meteor that forms a dim red mark in the night sky, one that most townspeople read as a sign for “Angel” but that one guilt-ridden minister reads very differently. That same minister secretly whips himself and fasts in private.
tossups.r: He is the secret father of the heroine’s daughter, Pearl. For 10 points, name this novel in which the Reverend Arthur Dimmesdale hides his role in Hester Prynne’s disgrace.

tossups.p: This novel’s heroine is questioned on the scaffold by the elder minister John Wilson during her public punishment. An old scholar who arrives in town that same day disguises his identity and becomes the town physician.
tossups.r: That physician, Roger Chillingworth, is secretly the heroine’s long-lost husband, and he spends the rest of the novel tormenting her lover. For 10 points, name this novel set in Puritan Boston.

tossups.p: A jailer named Master Brackett oversees the heroine’s imprisonment early in this novel. Its heroine’s husband was presumed lost at sea before unexpectedly arriving in Boston in disguise, calling himself Roger Chillingworth.
tossups.r: Chillingworth lodges with the minister Arthur Dimmesdale in order to secretly torment him. For 10 points, name this novel about Hester Prynne’s public shaming in colonial Massachusetts.

tossups.p: This novel’s heroine is a gifted seamstress whose elaborate needlework decorates the very mark she is forced to wear. Over time, the Puritan community reinterprets that mark, deciding it stands for “Able” rather than for her original sin.
tossups.r: Her daughter, Pearl, is often described by other characters as an “elf-child.” For 10 points, name this novel by Nathaniel Hawthorne.

tossups.p: In this novel’s climax, a minister publicly confesses his hidden sin on a scaffold and reveals a mark on his own chest before dying in the heroine’s arms. Pearl kisses her father for the first time in this scene, finally acknowledging him.
tossups.r: That minister, Arthur Dimmesdale, had spent years secretly tormented by the physician Roger Chillingworth. For 10 points, name this Hawthorne novel that ends with Dimmesdale’s public death.

tossups.p: Roger Chillingworth dies within a year of this novel’s climax and leaves his entire fortune to young Pearl. Shortly before that climax, this novel’s heroine had planned to flee Massachusetts by ship with her lover after meeting him in the forest.
tossups.r: She eventually returns to Boston alone and resumes wearing her mark voluntarily, becoming a counselor to troubled women. For 10 points, name this novel whose heroine is buried near Arthur Dimmesdale under a shared tombstone.

tossups.p: This novel opens with a long essay describing the narrator’s time working at a Salem customhouse, where he claims to have found an old manuscript. Its heroine, publicly shamed for adultery, refuses to name her child’s father even under pressure from Governor Bellingham.
tossups.r: That heroine’s husband arrives in town in disguise, calling himself Roger Chillingworth. For 10 points, name this novel about Hester Prynne’s punishment in Puritan Boston.

tossups.p: In one scene, Mistress Hibbins invites this novel’s guilt-ridden minister to a witches’ gathering, much as she once invited its heroine. That minister had earlier imagined seeing a meteor spell out a message directly above him.
tossups.r: Arthur Dimmesdale eventually confesses that he is the father of Hester Prynne’s daughter. For 10 points, name this Hawthorne novel.

tossups.p: This novel’s physician character disguises his true identity after being presumed dead at sea, taking lodging with the very minister he intends to torment. That minister, wracked with guilt, secretly fasts and keeps a midnight vigil on the public scaffold.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this novel in which Roger Chillingworth seeks revenge on Arthur Dimmesdale, the secret lover of his wife, Hester Prynne.

tossups.p: This novel’s heroine is sentenced to stand on a scaffold before the entire Puritan community, holding her infant daughter, Pearl. A physician who lodges with the colony’s minister secretly works to uncover that minister’s hidden sin.
tossups.r: The minister, Arthur Dimmesdale, is secretly Pearl’s father. For 10 points, name this novel set in seventeenth-century Boston.

tossups.p: This novel’s elf-like young character, Pearl, grows up without knowing her father’s identity for most of the story. Her mother, publicly shamed for adultery, becomes a skilled seamstress whose needlework is admired even as she is shunned.
tossups.r: Pearl’s father, a minister named Arthur Dimmesdale, is secretly tormented by the physician Roger Chillingworth. For 10 points, name this novel by Nathaniel Hawthorne.

tossups.p: A meteor’s dim light forms a mark across the sky on the same night that this novel’s guilt-ridden minister holds a midnight vigil on the public scaffold. Townspeople interpret the meteor as marking the recent death of Governor Winthrop.
tossups.r: That minister, Arthur Dimmesdale, cannot bring himself to confess publicly until the novel’s climax. For 10 points, name this novel about Hester Prynne and her forced public shaming.

tossups.p: This novel follows a woman forced to wear an embroidered mark of her sin, who refuses to name her child’s father before the Puritan magistrates of Boston. Its central family stands together at last when a dying minister confesses on the town scaffold.
tossups.r: Hester Prynne raises her daughter, Pearl, alone while her husband, Roger Chillingworth, seeks revenge on her former lover. For 10 points, name this Nathaniel Hawthorne novel.

clues.t: Its heroine, Hester Prynne, is forced to wear an embroidered mark of her sin in public
A novel by Nathaniel Hawthorne, published in 1850
Hester’s daughter, Pearl, is often called an “elf-child” by other characters
The Reverend Arthur Dimmesdale is secretly the father of Hester’s daughter
Roger Chillingworth, Hester’s estranged husband, hides his identity under a false name and works as a physician to torment Dimmesdale
Set in Puritan Boston in the seventeenth century
The introduction, “The Custom-House,” frames the story as a manuscript found by the narrator in a Salem customhouse
Mistress Hibbins, a rumored witch, invites Hester (and later Dimmesdale) to a witches’ gathering in the forest
A meteor forms a dim red mark in the sky, read by the town as a sign for “Angel” marking Governor Winthrop’s death, but read by Dimmesdale as a sign of his own guilt
On the scaffold, Hester is questioned by the elder minister John Wilson
The jailer Master Brackett guards Hester during her imprisonment
Hester’s skilled needlework and charity later lead some townspeople to reinterpret her mark as standing for “Able”
The story proper opens with Hester displayed on a public scaffold holding her infant daughter
Governor Bellingham presides over the Puritan colony and presses Hester to name her child’s father
Hester and Dimmesdale meet secretly in the forest, where she briefly removes her mark and unpins her hair
The couple briefly plans to flee the colony together on a ship, but Dimmesdale confesses publicly instead
Dimmesdale publicly confesses and reveals a mark on his own chest before dying in Hester’s arms
Pearl kisses her father for the first time during his public confession, finally acknowledging him
Chillingworth dies within a year of Dimmesdale’s death and leaves his fortune to Pearl
Hester eventually returns to Boston alone and resumes wearing her mark voluntarily, counseling troubled women
Hester is buried near Dimmesdale under a shared tombstone marked with a red letter A on a black background

trap.title: Which man is which?
trap.body: Two secretive men in Hester’s life are easy to mix up. Arthur Dimmesdale is her lover and Pearl’s real father, a guilt-ridden minister who cannot bring himself to confess. Roger Chillingworth is her husband, who hides his identity and works as a physician to secretly torment Dimmesdale.
trap.fix: A clue about secret guilt, fasting, or a vigil on the scaffold means Dimmesdale. A clue about disguise, medicine, or revenge means Chillingworth. Either way, remember this whole tossup is usually asking for the novel itself, not either man.
trap.line: Real answer line: The Scarlet Letter (also accept its full original title, The Scarlet Letter: A Romance).

qb.tip: A fourth Regular High School hit that matched this query was actually a tossup on “shipwrecks” that only name-drops this play in its giveaway — it’s excluded from the sample below. Caliban and the comic drunkards Stephano and Trinculo show up more often in the real clues than Prospero’s magic does.

sample.note: 5 real QBReader tossups (2 Middle School/Easy High School + 3 Regular High School, power-marked); a 4th Regular HS hit on a different answer line, “shipwrecks,” is excluded

tossups.p: This play’s title event strands a group of Neapolitan nobles returning from a royal wedding in Tunis on an enchanted island. Its sorcerer protagonist was set adrift on that same island twelve years earlier after his brother stole his title as Duke of Milan.
tossups.r: That protagonist’s spirit servant, Ariel, carries out his magic, while a monstrous servant named Caliban resents his control. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play featuring the magician Prospero.

tossups.p: This play’s airy spirit was once imprisoned inside a cloven pine tree by a witch named Sycorax [“SIK-uh-raks”] before being freed by the island’s new ruler. That same spirit later disguises itself as a harpy to torment a group of shipwrecked lords with an illusory feast.
tossups.r: Ariel ultimately helps Prospero reclaim his dukedom and reunite with the outside world. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play set on a magical island.

tossups.p: This play’s drunken butler, Stephano, is mistaken for a god who fell from the moon by the island’s monstrous native. That native joins Stephano and the jester Trinculo in a failed plot to murder the island’s ruler.
tossups.r: Caliban is the son of a dead witch named Sycorax. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play in which a magician named Prospero controls the spirit Ariel.

tossups.p: During a lavish masque celebrating a betrothal in this play, spirits appear as the goddesses Iris, Ceres, and Juno before the magician abruptly ends the celebration. That magician then declares that “our revels now are ended” and that people are “such stuff as dreams are made on.”
tossups.r: The betrothal is between his daughter Miranda and a shipwrecked prince, Ferdinand. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play.

tossups.p: Antonio and Sebastian plot to murder a sleeping king in this play, but Ariel wakes the old counselor Gonzalo in time to stop them. Years earlier, that same Gonzalo had secretly supplied this play’s protagonist with books as he was set adrift at sea.
tossups.r: The protagonist relies on those books for the sorcery that lets him conjure the storm that opens this play. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play starring the magician Prospero.

tossups.p: This play’s heroine has lived on an isolated island since early childhood and has barely seen any humans besides her father and a monstrous servant. Upon meeting a shipwrecked prince for the first time, she wonders aloud whether he might be “a spirit.”
tossups.r: That heroine, Miranda, soon falls in love with Ferdinand. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play in which Miranda’s father, Prospero, approves their marriage.

tossups.p: A spirit in this play sings “Full Fathom Five” to a prince who believes his father has drowned, though the king is secretly alive elsewhere on the island. This play’s title event is magically conjured to strand a group of Neapolitan and Milanese nobles.
tossups.r: That spirit, Ariel, serves the island’s exiled sorcerer. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play featuring the magician Prospero and the monster Caliban.

tossups.p: This play’s protagonist was deposed as Duke of Milan by his own brother, Antonio, and set adrift at sea with his infant daughter. Twelve years later, that protagonist uses sorcery to shipwreck his usurping brother on the same island where he found refuge.
tossups.r: He is aided by a spirit named Ariel and served, less willingly, by a monster named Caliban. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play about a magician’s revenge and forgiveness.

tossups.p: This play’s monstrous character is the son of a dead witch and resents being enslaved by the island’s ruler after once being taught language by that ruler’s daughter. He later tries, and fails, to lead a drunken rebellion against his master.
tossups.r: That character, Caliban, shares the island with a spirit named Ariel. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play in which the magician Prospero controls them both.

tossups.p: The poet W. H. Auden wrote a long response to this play called _The Sea and the Mirror_. In a famous postcolonial adaptation of this play by the writer Aimé Césaire [“eh-MAY say-ZEHR”], its monstrous character demands to be called “X.”
tossups.r: That monstrous character, Caliban, serves the magician Prospero alongside the spirit Ariel. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play.

tossups.p: In a 2010 film version of this play, Helen Mirren played a gender-swapped version of the sorcerer, while Djimon Hounsou played the monstrous Caliban. This play’s plot may draw on real accounts of a 1609 shipwreck in Bermuda.
tossups.r: Its sorcerer, Prospero, conjures the storm that gives this play its name. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play featuring the spirit Ariel.

tossups.p: Many scholars consider this to be the last play Shakespeare wrote entirely on his own, and its Epilogue has often been read as his farewell to the stage. In that Epilogue, the protagonist begs the audience to “set me free” with their applause.
tossups.r: That protagonist, the magician Prospero, ultimately chooses forgiveness over revenge. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play.

tossups.p: This play is unusual among Shakespeare’s works for taking place in a single location over the course of just a few hours. Its plot is set in motion when a magician conjures a storm to strand his usurping brother on his island of exile.
tossups.r: That magician, Prospero, is aided by the spirit Ariel and served by the monster Caliban. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play about a sorcerer’s island.

tossups.p: This play’s magician secretly arranges for his daughter to fall in love with the son of the king who helped usurp his dukedom years earlier. That magician ultimately forgives his enemies, vows to break his staff, and frees his spirit servant.
tossups.r: Prospero’s daughter Miranda is engaged to Ferdinand, the son of King Alonso, by the end of the play. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play featuring the monster Caliban.

tossups.p: This play opens with sailors struggling against a magically conjured storm that wrecks a ship carrying the King of Naples and his court. Its magician protagonist, exiled to a remote island twelve years earlier, uses that storm to bring his enemies within his power at last.
tossups.r: He is served by the spirit Ariel and the monster Caliban. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play in which Prospero gives up sorcery after reuniting his daughter Miranda with the outside world.

clues.t: Its magician protagonist, Prospero, is the exiled Duke of Milan
Caliban, a monstrous servant enslaved on the island, resents Prospero’s control
Ariel, a spirit of the air, carries out Prospero’s magic in exchange for eventual freedom
A magical storm, conjured by Prospero, shipwrecks his enemies on his island
Ends with Prospero’s daughter, Miranda, engaged to the shipwrecked prince Ferdinand
Antonio, Prospero’s brother, stole his dukedom and is among the shipwrecked nobles
Alonso, the King of Naples, searches the island for his son Ferdinand, believing him drowned
The drunken butler Stephano and jester Trinculo team up with Caliban against Prospero
Sycorax, Caliban’s dead mother, once ruled the island and imprisoned Ariel in a tree
After ending a wedding masque, Prospero declares that “we are such stuff as dreams are made on”
Prospero ultimately forgives his enemies, vows to break his magic staff, and frees Ariel
Gonzalo, an honest old counselor, is woken by Ariel in time to foil a murder plot against the sleeping King Alonso
Prospero was set adrift with infant Miranda and spent twelve years in exile before the play begins
Ariel sings “Full Fathom Five” to Ferdinand, who wrongly believes his father has drowned
In the Epilogue, Prospero asks the audience to “set me free” with their applause
Aldous Huxley’s _Brave New World_ takes its title from a line spoken by Miranda in this play
W. H. Auden’s long poem _The Sea and the Mirror_ responds to this play
A postcolonial adaptation by the writer Aimé Césaire reimagines Caliban demanding to be called “X”
Djimon Hounsou played Caliban in a 2010 film adaptation opposite Helen Mirren
Some scholars connect this play’s Act 4 wedding masque to a real royal wedding of its era
Unusually for Shakespeare, this play’s action unfolds in one place over just a few hours, following the classical unities

trap.title: Which monster, which spirit?
trap.body: Caliban and Ariel are easy to swap. Caliban is the earthy, resentful “monster” born on the island who wants Prospero gone; Ariel is the airy spirit who carries out Prospero’s magic in exchange for eventual freedom. Clues about drunken plotting or being enslaved point to Caliban; clues about songs, illusions, or flying point to Ariel.
trap.fix: Ask whether the clue describes a grudge and a wish to rebel (Caliban) or a magical task performed for Prospero (Ariel). Either way, the answer to this whole tossup is the play, not either character.

topics.briefing: William Shakespeare’s _King Lear_ opens with an aging king asking his three daughters to say how much they love him before he hands over his kingdom. Cordelia, the youngest, refuses to flatter him and is disinherited on the spot, while her sisters Goneril and Regan take her share and quickly turn on their father. Betrayed and homeless, the king wanders a storm-battered heath into madness, with his loyal Fool for company.

tossups.p: A nobleman in this play loses a trial by combat and admits that “the wheel is come full circle.” That same character, the illegitimate son of the Earl of Gloucester, earlier delivers a soliloquy beginning “Thou, Nature, art my goddess.”

tossups.p: The 17th-century playwright Nahum Tate rewrote this play with a happy ending in which a line promises that “truth and virtue shall at last succeed.” In the real version, the Duke of Cornwall blinds a nobleman for helping the exiled protagonist.
tossups.r: That blinded nobleman, the Earl of Gloucester, is then led by his disguised son to believe he has jumped off a cliff. For 10 points, name this Shakespearean tragedy about a king and his three daughters.

tossups.r: That storm comes after the protagonist’s daughters Goneril and Regan reduce his retinue of knights. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play in which an aging king disinherits his youngest daughter, Cordelia.

tossups.p: Disguised as a peasant, a nobleman’s son in this play kills Oswald, a steward loyal to Goneril. Earlier, as the beggar “Poor Tom,” that same son leads his own blinded father to believe he has jumped off a cliff, saving him from suicide.
tossups.r: That father, the Earl of Gloucester, had been blinded by the Duke of Cornwall for aiding the king. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play about a king who divides his kingdom among his three daughters.

tossups.p: A blinded nobleman in this play laments, “As flies to wanton boys are we to the gods; they kill us for their sport.” That same character is tricked by his disguised son into believing he has survived a fall from a cliff.
tossups.r: Meanwhile, the king’s Fool calls him “nuncle” as the two wander a storm-swept heath. For 10 points, name this Shakespearean tragedy in which an old king casts out his honest daughter, Cordelia.

tossups.p: The King of France marries this play’s youngest heroine despite her father disinheriting her without a dowry. That same heroine says she cannot “heave her heart into her mouth,” refusing to overstate her love for her father the way her sisters do.
tossups.r: Her sisters, Goneril and Regan, then turn against their father after dividing his kingdom between them. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play in which Cordelia is the only loyal daughter of the title ruler.

tossups.r: Meanwhile, Edmund, the Earl of Gloucester’s illegitimate son, frames his brother Edgar and is desired by both Goneril and Regan. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play about a king who divides his realm among his daughters.

tossups.p: The English poet John Keats wrote a sonnet about sitting down once again to reread this tragedy. In this play, a blinded nobleman is led by his disguised son, who pretends to be a beggar called “Poor Tom,” to believe he has jumped from a cliff.
tossups.r: That nobleman, the Earl of Gloucester, had been punished by the Duke of Cornwall for helping the title king. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play in which an old ruler is driven mad by his daughters.

tossups.p: Goneril and Regan, two sisters in this play, both desire the scheming Edmund; Goneril poisons her sister and then takes her own life. Edmund is fatally wounded in a duel with his legitimate brother, Edgar.
tossups.r: Earlier in this play, the sisters’ father divides his kingdom between them after disinheriting their honest younger sister, Cordelia. For 10 points, name this Shakespearean tragedy about an old king’s disastrous test of his daughters’ love.

tossups.p: This play’s Fool vanishes from the story without explanation after a final quip about going “to bed at noon.” Earlier, this play’s protagonist is reduced to holding a mock trial of a stool, which stands in for one of his cruel daughters.
tossups.r: That protagonist eventually dies of grief after his daughter Cordelia is put to death. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play in which an old king divides his realm among his three daughters.

The old king wanders onto a stormy heath, descending into madness, with his Fool for company
At the end, the old king dies of grief after his daughter Cordelia is put to death
Cordelia says she cannot “heave her heart into her mouth,” refusing to overstate her love the way her sisters do
The King of France marries Cordelia even though she has been disinherited and given no dowry
The Earl of Gloucester has two sons: the legitimate Edgar and the scheming, illegitimate Edmund
Disguised as the beggar “Poor Tom,” Edgar leads his own blinded father to believe he has jumped off a cliff, saving him from suicide
The Duke of Cornwall blinds the Earl of Gloucester as punishment for helping the exiled king
The king’s Fool offers witty, sorrowful commentary on his master’s choices, then vanishes from the play without explanation after Act III
Goneril and Regan both desire the scheming Edmund; Goneril poisons Regan and then takes her own life
Edmund is fatally wounded in a duel with his legitimate brother, Edgar
The loyal Earl of Kent is banished for objecting to the king’s harsh treatment of Cordelia, then disguises himself to keep serving him
“Nothing will come of nothing,” the king tells Cordelia after she will not flatter him like her sisters
After being blinded, Gloucester laments, “As flies to wanton boys are we to the gods; they kill us for their sport”

trap.title: Which tragic king, which daughter?
trap.body: Shakespeare wrote several tragedies about powerful men brought down by their own flaws, so don’t confuse this play with _Macbeth_, _Hamlet_, or _Othello_. Within the play itself, listen carefully for which daughter is being described: Cordelia is the loyal, disinherited one; Goneril and Regan are the flattering sisters who turn on their father.
trap.fix: If the clue names a Scottish king, a Danish prince, or a Moorish general, it is a different Shakespeare tragedy. If it names Cordelia, Goneril, or Regan, don’t answer with the daughter’s name — she is a character within this play, and the answer is the play itself.
trap.line: Real answer line: King Lear (also accept The Tragedy of King Lear or The History of King Lear).

topics.kicker: Virgil’s Roman epic · Rome’s own foundation myth
topics.briefing: After the Trojan War, a Trojan prince flees burning Troy carrying his father on his back, determined to find his people a new home. Blown off course to Carthage, he falls for Queen Dido before duty forces him onward to Italy, where his descendants will found Rome. Commissioned to give Rome its own epic to rival Homer’s, Virgil was still revising _the Aeneid_ when he died.

tossups.p: A Harpy named Celaeno curses this poem’s wandering travelers, warning that they will not found their city until hunger forces them to eat their own “tables.” Earlier, the priest Laocoon is killed by sea serpents after warning the Trojans not to trust a certain wooden horse.
tossups.r: This poem’s hero later visits the future site of Rome and receives a shield made by the god Vulcan showing the future Battle of Actium. For 10 points, name this Latin epic by Virgil about a Trojan prince’s journey to found Rome.

tossups.p: This poem’s hero loses his wife Creusa while fleeing burning Troy with his father on his back and his son at his side. Her ghost later appears to tell him to sail on without her.
tossups.r: Guided by the Sibyl of Cumae and a golden bough, this poem’s hero travels to the underworld in Book Six, where his father’s spirit previews the future glory of Rome. For 10 points, name this epic poem by Virgil.

tossups.p: During a royal hunt, a storm sent by Juno drives this poem’s hero into a cave with the Carthaginian queen he will later abandon. That queen, a widow of Sychaeus [“sih-KEE-us”], had fled to Africa and founded Carthage after her own brother Pygmalion murdered her husband.
tossups.r: Betrayed and heartbroken, that queen stabs herself with the hero’s own sword atop a funeral pyre. For 10 points, name this epic poem in which Dido falls in love with the title Trojan prince, written by Virgil.

tossups.p: This poem opens with the goddess Juno still furious over an old insult to her beauty, so she sends a storm to wreck this poem’s hero’s fleet near Carthage. In the underworld, this poem’s hero later meets the ghost of his helmsman Palinurus, who fell overboard while asleep at the rudder.
tossups.r: This poem begins, “I sing of arms and the man.” For 10 points, name this Roman epic about the journey of a Trojan refugee, written by Virgil.

tossups.p: In Book Two of this poem, the Greek spy Sinon convinces the Trojans to drag a massive wooden horse inside their walls, leading to the city’s fall. This poem’s hero then carries his father Anchises [“an-KY-seez”] out of the city on his back, losing his wife Creusa in the chaos.
tossups.r: That hero later fights Turnus, the king of the Rutulians, for the hand of the princess Lavinia. For 10 points, name this Roman epic, written by Virgil, that ends with its hero defeating Turnus.

tossups.p: This poem’s hero descends to the underworld and exits through the Gate of Ivory, reserved for false dreams, rather than the Gate of Horn. In an earlier book, he holds funeral games in Sicily to honor his dead father, during which despairing Trojan women try to burn his fleet.
tossups.r: This poem’s hero is the son of Venus and the mortal Anchises. For 10 points, name this epic poem by Virgil about the journey of this hero, a Trojan prince who becomes an ancestor of the Romans.

tossups.p: In this poem, the warrior maiden Camilla is killed by the warrior Arruns [“AR-unz”], who is then struck down by an arrow sent by the goddess Diana’s companion Opis. This poem’s hero kills Turnus in a rage after recognizing the belt of his slain ally Pallas.
tossups.r: At a temple in Carthage, this poem’s hero also sees a mural depicting the Trojan War, the first of several famous ekphrases [“EK-fruh-seez”] in the poem. For 10 points, name this Roman epic by Virgil.

tossups.p: Turnus’s sister Juturna [“yoo-TUR-na”] disguises herself as a charioteer to protect her brother from the single combat that ends this poem. Earlier, the son of this poem’s hero shoots a tame stag while hunting, sparking a war in Italy.
tossups.r: This poem’s hero abandons Dido, the queen of Carthage, to continue his voyage toward Italy. For 10 points, name this epic in which a Trojan prince’s descendants go on to found Rome, written by Virgil.

tossups.p: Virgil was reportedly still revising this poem when he died, having modeled it on Homer’s epics to glorify the new Roman emperor Augustus. A Harpy named Celaeno predicts that this poem’s travelers will found their city only after they are forced to eat bread used as tables.
tossups.r: This poem’s hero loses his wife Creusa while escaping the burning city of Troy. For 10 points, name this Latin epic about a Trojan refugee who becomes the ancestor of the Romans.

tossups.p: This poem contains an extended simile comparing the builders of a great city to bees at work in a hive. Its hero is guided by the Sibyl of Cumae and a golden bough into the underworld, where he glimpses the future heroes of Rome.
tossups.r: A storm sent by Juno first drives this poem’s hero to Carthage, where Queen Dido falls in love with him. For 10 points, name this epic poem by Virgil, which ends with its hero’s defeat of Turnus.

tossups.p: This poem’s hero’s fleet is wrecked by a storm after Juno bribes the wind god Aeolus with the promise of a nymph bride. Later, this hero’s helmsman Palinurus nods off at the rudder and tumbles overboard.
tossups.r: This hero eventually kills Turnus to win the hand of Lavinia, ending a war in Latium. For 10 points, name this Roman national epic by Virgil, which recounts the journey of a Trojan prince toward Italy.

tossups.p: This poem’s hero carries the household gods of Troy, along with his father Anchises, as he flees the city after Sinon’s wooden horse trick succeeds. Later, at Carthage, that hero’s grieving lover takes her own life with his sword atop a funeral pyre.
tossups.r: Virgil begins this poem with the line “I sing of arms and the man.” For 10 points, name this Roman epic about a Trojan refugee whose descendants go on to found Rome.

tossups.p: In this poem, the Fury Allecto helps incite a war in Italy after the hero’s son kills a tame stag belonging to a local herdsman’s daughter. This poem’s hero had earlier left the underworld through an ivory gate reserved for false dreams.
tossups.r: This poem’s hero battles Turnus for the right to marry Lavinia, daughter of King Latinus. For 10 points, name this Latin epic by Virgil, which recounts a Trojan prince’s journey toward the founding of Rome.

tossups.p: This poem’s hero marvels at a shield forged by Vulcan, decorated with scenes of Roman history including the future Battle of Actium. He receives that shield after visiting Evander at the future site of Rome.
tossups.r: This poem’s hero falls in love with Dido, the queen of Carthage, before duty calls him onward to Italy. For 10 points, name this epic poem about a survivor of the fall of Troy, written by Virgil.

tossups.p: This poem’s hero escapes the burning city of Troy carrying his father Anchises on his back and leading his young son by the hand. He later falls in love with Dido, the queen of Carthage, before leaving her to continue his journey.
tossups.r: This poem’s hero eventually settles in Italy, where his descendants will found the city of Rome. For 10 points, name this Latin epic poem written by the Roman poet Virgil.

clues.t: Latin epic poem written by the Roman poet Virgil (Publius Vergilius Maro)
Follows a Trojan prince, son of the goddess Venus and the mortal Anchises, who flees fallen Troy
Hero’s descendants become the ancestors of the Romans; written to glorify the emperor Augustus
Hero falls in love with Dido, queen of Carthage, who kills herself after he leaves her for Italy
Opens with the line “I sing of arms and the man” (Latin: “Arma virumque cano”)
Hero loses his wife Creusa while escaping burning Troy; her ghost later appears to him
Guided into the underworld in Book Six by the Sibyl of Cumae using a golden bough
In the underworld, his father Anchises shows him a pageant of future Roman heroes
In Italy, wages war against Turnus, king of the Rutulians, for the hand of princess Lavinia
The poem ends abruptly with the hero killing Turnus in single combat
Left unfinished at Virgil’s death; he had reportedly worked on it for about ten years
Modeled on Homer’s epics to give Rome its own national founding story under Augustus
Book Two: the Greek Sinon tricks the Trojans into bringing in a wooden horse; the priest Laocoon is killed by sea serpents for warning against it
Carries his father Anchises on his back and leads his son Ascanius (also called Iulus) out of burning Troy
The Harpy Celaeno curses the travelers, predicting they’ll found their city only after eating bread used as “tables”
Dido stabs herself with the hero’s own sword atop a funeral pyre after he sails for Italy
Holds funeral games in Sicily for his dead father Anchises; grieving Trojan women try to burn the fleet
His helmsman Palinurus falls asleep at the rudder and tumbles overboard; the hero later meets his ghost in the underworld
Leaves the underworld through the Gate of Ivory, reserved for false dreams, instead of the Gate of Horn
War breaks out in Italy after his son, out hunting, kills a tame stag belonging to a herdsman’s daughter
At a temple in Carthage, the hero sees a mural depicting the Trojan War, one of the poem’s famous ekphrases
Vulcan forges the hero a shield decorated with Roman history, including the future Battle of Actium
The warrior maiden Camilla is killed by Arruns, who is then struck down by Diana’s companion Opis
Enraged after recognizing the belt of his slain ally Pallas, the hero kills Turnus while Turnus wears it
Turnus’s divine sister Juturna disguises herself as a charioteer to protect him from the final duel
Dido’s dead husband Sychaeus was murdered by her own brother Pygmalion, driving her to flee Tyre and found Carthage

trap.title: The hero, or his epic?
trap.body: Quiz bowl sometimes asks for “Aeneas” (the Trojan hero) and sometimes for “The Aeneid” (Virgil’s poem about him) — they are two different answer lines, even though one real tossup on Aeneas still accepted “The Aeneid” as an alternate. A clue about the golden bough, Dido, or the fall of Troy could be building toward either one.
trap.fix: Listen for the noun. “This hero,” “this prince,” or “this man” usually wants Aeneas. “This poem,” “this epic,” or “this work” wants The Aeneid.
trap.line: Real answer line: The Aeneid (or Aeneis); a related tossup’s line: Aeneas (accept The Aeneid)

topics.kicker: Harper Lee’s novel · Racial injustice seen through a child’s eyes
topics.briefing: Through the eyes of young Scout Finch, this novel follows her father Atticus as he defends a Black man falsely accused of a crime he didn’t commit in 1930s Alabama. Scout and her brother Jem also spend the story chasing rumors about their mysterious, reclusive neighbor, Boo Radley. Harper Lee’s only novel for over fifty years, it won the Pulitzer Prize and remains one of the most-read books in American schools.

sample.note: the 12 real QBReader tossups for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked)

tossups.p: A reclusive neighbor in this novel is rumored to have once stabbed his own father with a pair of scissors. That neighbor, Arthur “Boo” Radley, leaves small gifts like soap figures and a pocket watch for two children in the knothole of a tree.
tossups.r: Those children’s father, a small-town lawyer, defends a Black man falsely accused of attacking a white woman named Mayella Ewell. For 10 points, name this novel about Scout and Jem Finch, written by Harper Lee.

tossups.p: A neighbor in this novel makes one character read aloud to her every afternoon as punishment for destroying her camellia bushes; that neighbor turns out to be a morphine addict named Mrs. Dubose. Later, the narrator calms an angry mob outside the jailhouse by asking Mr. Cunningham about his son.
tossups.r: The narrator’s father, attorney Atticus Finch, then defends Tom Robinson against a false charge brought by Mayella and Bob Ewell. For 10 points, name this novel narrated by young Scout Finch.

tossups.p: This novel’s narrator watches her father in court from the balcony reserved for Black spectators, alongside her brother and her friend Dill Harris. Her father once calmly shoots a rabid dog named Tim Johnson with a single blast, revealing why he had been nicknamed “One-Shot” as a boy.
tossups.r: That father, Atticus Finch, defends Tom Robinson at a racially charged trial in Maycomb, Alabama. For 10 points, name this novel by Harper Lee.

tossups.p: At the climax of this novel, a drunken man named Bob Ewell attacks two children walking home from a school pageant, where one of them had been dressed as a ham. A reclusive neighbor intervenes and carries an injured boy home to his father.
tossups.r: That neighbor, Arthur “Boo” Radley, is credited with saving Jem and Scout’s lives. For 10 points, name this novel by Harper Lee, set in the fictional town of Maycomb, Alabama.

tossups.p: A lawyer in this novel defends a disabled Black man whose left arm was crippled in a cotton-gin accident years earlier, a detail that undercuts the charge against him. Despite that evidence, an all-white jury convicts the defendant anyway.
tossups.r: That defendant, Tom Robinson, is later shot while trying to escape from prison. For 10 points, name this novel in which lawyer Atticus Finch takes on a doomed case in the Jim Crow South.

tossups.p: A family scorned by its neighbors as the poorest in town, headed by the violent, grudge-holding Bob Ewell, brings a false accusation against a hardworking Black field hand in this novel. That man’s employer, Link Deas, later threatens to invoke the “Ladies’ Law” to protect his widow.
tossups.r: The accused man, Tom Robinson, is defended at trial by Atticus Finch. For 10 points, name this novel narrated by Finch’s young daughter, Scout.

tossups.p: A man named Dolphus Raymond pretends to be a hopeless drunk, sipping Coca-Cola from a paper bag, so that his Maycomb neighbors will have an excuse for why he lives among Black families in this novel. Aunt Alexandra moves in with the narrator’s family partway through the story.
tossups.r: The narrator’s brother, Jem, is injured defending her from Bob Ewell near the novel’s end. For 10 points, name this novel about Scout and Jem Finch, written by Harper Lee.

tossups.p: This novel opens with its narrator recalling how her brother badly broke his arm when he was nearly thirteen, then flashes back to introduce Dill Harris, a visiting friend obsessed with the mysterious Radley house down the street. Its narrator and her brother find chewing gum, pennies, and carved soap figures hidden in a tree’s knothole.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this novel narrated by Jean Louise “Scout” Finch, in which her father Atticus defends Tom Robinson.

tossups.p: This novel’s title comes from a lesson its narrator’s father teaches about a harmless songbird that does nothing but sing — a creature it would be a sin to harm. A kindly neighbor, Miss Maudie Atkinson, loses her house to a fire one winter night.
tossups.r: That lesson comes to apply to both Tom Robinson and the reclusive Boo Radley. For 10 points, name this novel by Harper Lee, set in Depression-era Alabama.

tossups.p: Decades after this novel was published, an earlier draft of it reached shelves as the controversial “sequel” _Go Set a Watchman_, which depicts its narrator as an adult. In this novel, the narrator’s housekeeper, a Black woman named Calpurnia, helps raise her and her brother.
tossups.r: That narrator’s father, Atticus Finch, defends Tom Robinson, falsely accused of attacking Mayella Ewell. For 10 points, name this novel set in Maycomb, Alabama.

tossups.p: This novel’s narrator gets into a fistfight with her cousin Francis at Christmas after he insults her father’s choice of clients. That father calmly shoots a rabid dog, Tim Johnson, in the street, revealing a marksmanship skill his children never knew he had.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this novel in which attorney Atticus Finch defends Tom Robinson and raises his children, Jem and Scout, in Maycomb, Alabama.

tossups.p: This novel’s young narrator helps calm a mob gathered outside the county jail by chatting with Walter Cunningham about his son, not realizing the danger she has defused. Her father had been sitting outside that same jail to guard his client.
tossups.r: That client, Tom Robinson, still loses his case to an all-white jury despite clear proof of his innocence. For 10 points, name this novel by Harper Lee.

tossups.p: This novel’s narrator finds an unexpected blanket around her shoulders on a cold night while watching a neighbor’s house burn down, and only later do she and her brother realize their mysterious neighbor Boo Radley had put it there himself.
tossups.r: That same neighbor later saves the narrator and her brother from a nighttime attack by Bob Ewell. For 10 points, name this novel by Harper Lee, narrated by Scout Finch.

tossups.p: This novel’s central trial turns on evidence that its defendant’s left arm is essentially useless, making it unlikely he delivered the blows described by his accuser. That accuser’s father, Bob Ewell, spends the rest of the novel plotting revenge on the defense attorney’s family.
tossups.r: The defendant, Tom Robinson, is nonetheless convicted. For 10 points, name this novel in which Atticus Finch takes on Robinson’s doomed defense.

tossups.p: This novel follows two children, Jem and Scout Finch, growing up in the small Alabama town of Maycomb during the Great Depression. Their father, a widowed lawyer named Atticus Finch, agrees to defend a Black man falsely accused of a crime against a white woman.
tossups.r: Their mysterious neighbor, Boo Radley, eventually saves the children’s lives. For 10 points, name this novel by Harper Lee.

Narrated by young Scout Finch (Jean Louise Finch)
Scout’s father, lawyer Atticus Finch, is the moral center of the novel

Nicknamed “One-Shot,” Atticus kills a rabid dog named Tim Johnson with a single shot

Jem is forced to read aloud to the morphine-addicted Mrs. Dubose after destroying her camellia bushes
Calpurnia, the Finches’ Black housekeeper, helps raise Scout and Jem
Aunt Alexandra moves in with the Finch family partway through the novel
Dolphus Raymond fakes being a drunk, sipping Coca-Cola from a paper bag, to excuse living among Black neighbors
Tom Robinson’s employer, Link Deas, later threatens to invoke the “Ladies’ Law” to protect his widow
An earlier draft was published in 2015 as the controversial novel _Go Set a Watchman_
Rumored to have once stabbed his father with a pair of scissors, Boo Radley has not been seen in public for years
Kind neighbor Miss Maudie Atkinson’s house burns down one winter night
The Ewells, including Bob and his daughter Mayella, are the poorest, most looked-down-on family in Maycomb

trap.title: This novel, or its “sequel”?
trap.body: An early draft of this novel was published in 2015 as _Go Set a Watchman_, featuring an adult Jean Louise “Scout” Finch returning home from New York and a very different, more old-fashioned Atticus. The two books share characters and a setting but very different plots and reputations.
trap.fix: A child narrator, the Tom Robinson trial, or Boo Radley means _To Kill a Mockingbird_. A grown-up Scout visiting Maycomb from New York means _Go Set a Watchman_.
trap.line: Real answer line: To Kill a Mockingbird

topics.name: The Red Badge of Courage
topics.kicker: Stephen Crane’s Civil War novel · A soldier’s private battle with fear
topics.briefing: Young Henry Fleming marches off to fight in the American Civil War dreaming of glory, then panics and runs during his very first battle. Ashamed, he wanders battlefields full of the dead and wounded before a head wound from a panicked comrade’s rifle lets him return to his regiment with his secret intact. Stephen Crane, who had never seen a battle himself, wrote this short, vivid novel about fear, guilt, and growing up in war.

tossups.p: An officer in this novel insults one regiment as nothing more than “mule drivers” and “mud diggers,” spurring them to fight harder later on. Earlier, this novel’s protagonist feels his eyeballs are “about to crack like hot stones.”
tossups.r: That protagonist, Henry Fleming, panics and flees into the forest during the fighting. For 10 points, name this Civil War novel by Stephen Crane.

tossups.p: This novel’s protagonist wanders past a column of wounded men, including a “tattered soldier” who keeps painfully asking about a wound the protagonist does not actually have. In a quiet forest clearing, that protagonist stumbles upon the body of a dead soldier propped against a tree.
tossups.r: Fleeing his regiment, Henry is struck on the head by a fellow Union soldier’s rifle butt during the chaos. For 10 points, name this novel by Stephen Crane.

tossups.p: This novel’s “tall soldier,” Jim Conklin, dies of his wounds in a field, convulsing dramatically as the sun is compared to a wafer in the sky. The protagonist, overwhelmed with guilt, abandons the tattered soldier who had been asking about his injury.
tossups.r: That protagonist, Henry Fleming, later lies about how he was struck on the head. For 10 points, name this Civil War novel by Stephen Crane.

tossups.p: A soldier named Wilson gives this novel’s protagonist a packet of letters to deliver to his family before a battle, then sheepishly asks for them back after surviving. Wilson also bandages the protagonist’s head wound, never learning how it really happened.
tossups.r: That protagonist, Henry Fleming, eventually matures into a capable soldier himself. For 10 points, name this novel by Stephen Crane.

tossups.p: This novel’s protagonist is struck on the head by a fleeing comrade’s rifle butt, a wound that his comrades mistake for a bullet graze. The protagonist lets his regiment believe he was shot rather than admit he deserted during the fighting.
tossups.r: Guilt over that lie haunts Henry Fleming even as he grows into a steadier soldier. For 10 points, name this Stephen Crane novel set during the Civil War.

tossups.p: This novel’s protagonist and a soldier named Wilson win an officer’s praise for their reckless bravery in a charge late in the story. Earlier, that protagonist had thrown a pinecone at a squirrel while fleeing through the woods, trying to prove to himself that nature fears death too.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this novel in which Henry Fleming eventually becomes his regiment’s flag-bearer, written by Stephen Crane.

tossups.p: This novel’s protagonist watches his friend Jim Conklin, called “the tall soldier,” die in a field after a final, terrible convulsion. Later, the protagonist fights another soldier, Wilson, over the honor of carrying their regiment’s flag in a desperate charge.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this Civil War novel about the Union soldier Henry Fleming, written by Stephen Crane.

tossups.p: This novel’s fictional 304th New York regiment is sent on what seems like a suicidal charge, during which its original flag-bearer falls and the protagonist grabs the colors himself. Wilson, once called “the loud soldier,” captures an enemy flag in a later charge.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this novel in which Henry Fleming overcomes his fear to fight bravely for the Union, written by Stephen Crane.

tossups.p: This novel never names the battle its fictional regiment fights, though historians usually identify it with the Battle of Chancellorsville. Walking among the wounded after fleeing, its protagonist secretly longs for a wound of his own to prove his bravery.
tossups.r: That protagonist, Henry Fleming, instead gets an unheroic head wound from a fleeing comrade’s rifle. For 10 points, name this Civil War novel by Stephen Crane.

tossups.p: This novel’s author also wrote the shipwreck story _The Open Boat_ and the grim city novel _Maggie: A Girl of the Streets_. Its own subtitle calls it “An Episode of the American Civil War.”
tossups.r: Its protagonist, Henry Fleming, flees his first battle out of sheer terror. For 10 points, name this naturalistic novel by Stephen Crane.

tossups.p: A loud, boastful soldier named Wilson hands this novel’s protagonist a packet of letters before a battle, certain that he will die. That same soldier later calms down and tends the protagonist’s head wound, never learning its embarrassing cause.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this novel whose protagonist, Henry Fleming, eventually becomes a flag-bearer for the Union, written by Stephen Crane.

topics.kicker: T. S. Eliot’s 1922 modernist poem · Reinvented English poetry out of fragments
topics.briefing: T. S. Eliot’s _The Waste Land_ (1922) reads like a radio dial spinning through a ruined world: a tarot reading, a London pub at closing time, a boat on the Thames, and lines in German, French, and Sanskrit all crash together without warning. Eliot’s friend Ezra Pound cut the original draft nearly in half. The poem opens by mocking springtime itself — “April is the cruellest month” — and ends, just as suddenly, with a Sanskrit word for peace said three times.

topics.name: The Adventures of Tom Sawyer
topics.kicker: Mark Twain’s mischievous boy hero · A classic American boyhood adventure
topics.briefing: Mark Twain based _The Adventures of Tom Sawyer_ (1876) on his own boyhood memories of growing up along the Mississippi River in Hannibal, Missouri. Tom tricks his friends into whitewashing Aunt Polly’s fence, falls for the judge’s daughter Becky Thatcher, and gets lost in a cave where the murderous Injun Joe is hiding. Twain later let Tom’s best friend, Huckleberry Finn, narrate an even more famous novel of his own.

tossups.p: This character tricks a group of neighborhood boys into trading him treasures for the privilege of whitewashing a fence. He later runs away with two friends to Jackson’s Island to live as pirates, letting the whole town believe the boys have drowned.
tossups.r: He then sneaks into his own funeral to watch his grieving Aunt Polly mourn him. For 10 points, name this title character, a friend of Huckleberry Finn, in a novel by Mark Twain.

tossups.p: While out at midnight to test a wart cure, this character secretly watches the drunkard Muff Potter get framed for a murder actually committed by Injun Joe. Months later, this character finally testifies in court to clear Potter’s name.
tossups.r: He later gets lost in a cave with Becky Thatcher and spots Injun Joe hiding there. For 10 points, name this character created by Mark Twain.

tossups.p: This character trades his whitewashing loot for colored tickets so he can win a Bible at Sunday school, then ruins the moment by answering “David and Goliath” when asked to name Jesus’s first two disciples. He also takes a whipping for a page torn from the schoolmaster’s anatomy book.

topics.name: The Divine Comedy
topics.kicker: Dante’s journey through the afterlife · Medieval Europe’s great epic poem
topics.briefing: Exiled from his beloved Florence and never allowed to return, Dante Alighieri built an entire afterlife instead. In _The Divine Comedy_, the spirit of the Roman poet Virgil guides a lost, frightened Dante down through nine circles of Hell and up the mountain of Purgatory, at whose summit Dante’s long-lost love, Beatrice, takes over as his guide into Heaven. All three parts end on the very same word: the Italian for “stars.”

tossups.p: In this poem, the Roman poet Virgil guides the narrator through the first two of its three parts before giving way to Beatrice, who leads him through the third. A gate near the start of the journey bears the warning “Abandon all hope, ye who enter here.”
tossups.r: Its first part organizes Hell into nine circles, each one devoted to a different kind of sin. For 10 points, name this three-part epic by Dante Alighieri, which also includes Purgatorio and Paradiso.

tossups.p: Early in this poem, a spirit discusses Florence’s rival Black and White Guelph political factions with the narrator. Dante Alighieri wrote much of this work while exiled from that same city. Its final part has Beatrice guide the narrator through the heavenly spheres.
tossups.r: That final part ends with a vision of three overlapping circles of light in the Empyrean. For 10 points, name this three-part poem whose first part, Inferno, follows Virgil and Dante through nine circles of Hell.

tossups.p: This poem’s narrator is first blocked in a dark wood by a leopard, a lion, and a she-wolf before Virgil arrives to guide him. Deep inside Hell, a giant three-headed Lucifer sits frozen in ice at the very center of the ninth circle.
tossups.r: The narrator’s journey continues upward into Purgatorio and finally Paradiso, where Beatrice takes over as guide. For 10 points, name this three-part epic poem by Dante.

tossups.p: The monster Geryon carries this poem’s narrator down to a lower circle, and an angel must open the gates of the walled City of Dis before he can continue. Earlier, the doomed lovers Paolo and Francesca are swept up together forever for falling in love when they should not have.
tossups.r: Its narrator is guided first by Virgil and later by Beatrice. For 10 points, name this three-canticle poem by Dante Alighieri.

tossups.p: Fortune-tellers in this poem’s underworld are punished by being forced to walk forever with their heads turned backward. At the very bottom of that underworld, Lucifer’s three mouths hold history’s three most notorious traitors: Brutus, Cassius, and Judas.
tossups.r: That underworld, Inferno, is only the first of this poem’s three parts, which also include Purgatorio and Paradiso. For 10 points, name this epic poem by Dante Alighieri.

tossups.p: A gate in this poem warns “Abandon all hope, ye who enter here.” Nearby, the self-serving souls of history’s fence-sitters cry out in Hell’s vestibule, never allowed to cross the river Acheron into Hell proper.
tossups.r: This poem later follows its narrator up the mountain of Purgatory and into the heavenly spheres of Paradiso. For 10 points, name this three-part epic by Dante Alighieri, whose first part is Inferno.

tossups.p: A demon named Malacoda lies to this poem’s travelers about a bridge being intact over one of Hell’s ditches. In this same poem’s final canto, Beatrice has already given way to Saint Bernard as the narrator glimpses three overlapping circles of light in the Empyrean.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this three-part poem in which Dante Alighieri journeys through Inferno, Purgatorio, and Paradiso.

tossups.p: The medieval theologian Saint Bonaventure appears to this poem’s narrator in the heavenly sphere of the Sun. Earlier in the same poem, that narrator’s path through a dark wood is blocked by a leopard, a lion, and a she-wolf.
tossups.r: Virgil then arrives to guide him through Inferno and Purgatorio. For 10 points, name this three-part epic poem by Dante.

tossups.p: Souls in this poem’s Purgatorio are heard chanting the Latin psalm “In exitu Israel de Aegypto.” Much earlier, a gate warns the narrator to “abandon all hope,” and he soon finds Hell divided into nine circles, each one devoted to a different kind of sin.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this epic poem whose narrator, Dante, is guided by Virgil and then by Beatrice.

tossups.p: Lucifer’s three mouths hold history’s three most notorious traitors — Brutus, Cassius, and Judas — at the very bottom of this poem’s Hell. All three parts of this poem end on the exact same Italian word, “stelle,” meaning stars.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this three-part epic in which Dante Alighieri travels through Inferno, Purgatorio, and Paradiso.

tossups.p: A giant three-headed Lucifer is frozen in ice at the exact center of this poem’s Hell. Far above, in this same poem’s Paradiso, the narrator glimpses three overlapping circles of light in the Empyrean.
tossups.r: Virgil and later Beatrice guide the narrator between these two settings. For 10 points, name this three-part poem by Dante Alighieri.

tossups.p: This poem’s doomed lovers Paolo and Francesca are punished together forever for a love affair they should not have had. A gate elsewhere in the same work warns “Abandon all hope,” above Hell’s nine circles of sin.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this three-part epic whose narrator, guided first by Virgil, eventually reaches Paradiso with Beatrice.

tossups.p: This poem’s narrator loses his way in a dark wood on Good Friday before Virgil appears to guide him. At the very bottom of this poem’s Hell, Lucifer’s three mouths hold Brutus, Cassius, and Judas.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this three-part poem that also includes Purgatorio and Paradiso, written by Dante Alighieri.

tossups.p: This poem’s narrator rides the monster Geryon down toward a lower circle, where he later sees fortune-tellers forced to walk with their heads turned backward. Much later, Beatrice guides the same narrator through the heavenly spheres of Paradiso.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this three-canticle epic poem by Dante Alighieri.

tossups.p: An angel must open the gates of the City of Dis before this poem’s narrator and his guide Virgil can continue deeper into Hell. All three parts of this poem — Inferno, Purgatorio, and Paradiso — end with the same word, the Italian word for stars.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this epic poem written by the medieval Italian poet Dante Alighieri.

clues.t: Written by the medieval Italian poet Dante Alighieri
Divided into three parts — Inferno, Purgatorio, and Paradiso — covering Hell, Purgatory, and Heaven
The Roman poet Virgil serves as the narrator’s guide through the first two parts of the journey
Hell is organized into nine circles, each one punishing a different category of sin
A gate leading into Hell bears the warning “Abandon all hope, ye who enter here”
Dante’s idealized love, Beatrice, takes over from Virgil as his guide for the final part of the journey, into Heaven
Each of the poem’s three parts ends on the same Italian word, “stelle,” meaning stars
At the very center of Hell, a giant three-headed Lucifer is trapped in ice
Lucifer’s three mouths hold history’s three worst traitors, Brutus, Cassius, and Judas
The doomed lovers Paolo and Francesca are swept up together forever, unable to part
Dante’s path is first blocked in a dark wood by a leopard, a lion, and a she-wolf
Dante wrote much of this poem in exile, after politics in his home city of Florence turned against him
The monster Geryon carries Dante and Virgil down to a lower circle on its back
Fortune-tellers are punished by being forced to walk forever with their heads turned backward
An angel must open the gates of the City of Dis, a walled fortress deep inside Hell, before the journey can continue
The poem’s journey famously begins on Good Friday
The medieval theologian Saint Bonaventure appears in the heavenly sphere of the Sun
The self-serving souls of history’s fence-sitters cry out in Hell’s vestibule, never allowed to cross the river Acheron into Hell proper
A demon named Malacoda lies about a bridge being intact over one of Hell’s ditches
A spirit discusses the rival Black and White Guelph political factions of Florence early in the journey
The very last canto describes three overlapping circles of light in the Empyrean, the highest heaven
Souls in Purgatorio are heard chanting the Latin psalm “In exitu Israel de Aegypto”

trap.title: Whole poem, or just Inferno?
trap.body: Most real tossups on Dante’s hellish imagery — the nine circles, Virgil as guide, “Abandon all hope” — are actually asking for Inferno alone, which is only the poem’s first third, with a prompt if you say “Divine Comedy.” Purgatorio and Paradiso are the other two parts, and a tossup on the whole poem has to reach into one of them.
trap.fix: If every clue is about Hell, sinners, and Virgil with no mention of Purgatorio, Paradiso, or Beatrice, the safer buzz is “Inferno.” Wait for the poem to leave Hell — a mountain of Purgatory, the heavenly spheres, or Beatrice taking over as guide — before buzzing “Divine Comedy.”
trap.line: Real answer line: The Divine Comedy (or Divina Commedia); a related tossup’s line: Inferno (prompt on Divine Comedy)
